title: The 1% fee that eats a third of your pension
description:
A fee too small to notice, compounding for forty years. Here is what one percent actually costs.

New video every day.

scenes.say: You picked the right fund. You held it for forty years. And you still lost almost a third of it.
Not to a crash. To a fee of one percent a year. A number so small it looks like a rounding error.
Here is why it is not. The fee does not come out of your gains. It comes out of your balance, every single year, including the years you are down.
So it does not subtract. It compounds, in the wrong direction. Over forty years, one percent a year quietly removes about thirty percent of what you would have had.
A fund returning seven percent that charges one is not beating a fund returning six that charges nothing. It is the same fund with a worse ending.
Fees are the one part of investing you actually control. Follow for more money ideas explained simply.
